identity_boundary_incidents_during_cerem.cause: sudo inherited the operator's interactive shell PATH (no secure_path in this host's sudoers); several PATH entries ahead of /bin are owned/writable by the configured agent principal (uid 501), so the fail-closed ACL-trust-tool resolver (hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py::_resolve_trusted_executable_for_subject) correctly refused to trust ls/getfacl rather than silently treating the indeterminate ACL state as safe
identity_boundary_incidents_during_cerem.resolution: operator re-ran with `sudo env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin ...` (a minimal trusted PATH) -- no source change
identity_boundary_incidents_during_cerem.classification: environmental invocation issue, not a code defect; no src/pcae change

identity_boundary_incidents_during_cerem.cause: env -i also clears HOME, which is how Python's user-site mechanism locates ~/Library/Python/3.14/lib/python/site-packages (where fido2 is installed for this interpreter)
identity_boundary_incidents_during_cerem.resolution: operator added `PYTHONPATH=/Users/atilamadai/Library/Python/3.14/lib/python/site-packages` alongside the minimal PATH -- does not affect the OS PATH the ACL-trust check inspects

identity_boundary_incidents_during_cerem.issue: an ad hoc independent read-only verification script (HumanPrincipalRegistryStore.production() called directly, not via production_writer()) raised HPACAuthorityError: production HPAC root is not protected from the configured agent principal (root=agent_is_owner_with_write_bit)
identity_boundary_incidents_during_cerem.cause: HPACStoreAuthority._validate_production_boundary() checks writability against self._configured_agent_identity if bound, else falls back to _current_agent_identity() (the live process euid). _configured_agent_identity is only ever bound inside production_writer()'s recognition sequence for a specific mutating PawaOperation. A standalone script calling HumanPrincipalRegistryStore.production() directly (even though invoked as root, the correct deployment owner) is evaluated against root's own ambient identity, which trivially owns the protected root -> the boundary check fails closed, exactly as designed to prevent the protection guarantee being asserted vacuously
identity_boundary_incidents_during_cerem.resolution: abandoned the ad hoc script; verification was instead performed via plain filesystem `cat`/`ls` as root (bypasses the Python authority layer entirely -- no HPACStoreAuthority involved, therefore no boundary check to trip, and no new authority invented)
identity_boundary_incidents_during_cerem.classification: genuine architectural gap: no canonical read-only production-boundary-safe inspection path exists outside an active production_writer() transaction. Not repaired in this phase (would require a src/pcae change, out of scope; the phase-defined completion of the write ceremonies already performs their own correctly-bound internal read-back per RHAMP-REQ-025 / HPAC-REQ-015, which is why they succeeded and printed their `enrolled ...` lines rather than raising). Recorded here as a finding for a future phase, not fabricated as C-1-blocking since the actual production write path already satisfies the read-back requirement internally.
